Subject: Pilot contract question — auto-renew for pilots

Hi Neha / Priyom,

Quick question as we're reviewing the latest order form: for this 6-month pilot we asked Legal to keep an opt-out rather than an automatic renewal, but the redline still has an auto-renew clause (Section 2.1). Can you confirm if Redwood will agree to a one-time waiver of auto-renew specifically for pilots under $50k ARR? We need a clean stop so our procurement doesn't auto-commit spend.

Also, our procurement team prefers a 60-day notice window for any renewal (instead of 90) for pilot-stage agreements. Is there flexibility there?

We're hoping to finalize by EOW so we can kick off the pilot on Aug 15.

Thanks,
Jenny Park
Sr. Product Ops | Acme Inc.

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Pilot contract question — legal take

Neha / Priyom — legal quick-take below.

Summary: we can agree to a narrow, temporal waiver for auto-renew on the order form that references the MSA but does not amend it permanently. Suggested language: "Notwithstanding Section 2.1, the Order Form for the Acme Inc. Pilot dated Aug 2026 shall not automatically renew at the end of the Term; any further services shall be subject to a new Order Form or an executed amendment. This waiver applies only to the Order Form between Redwood and Acme Inc. for the 6-month pilot and expires upon the earlier of (a) execution of a subsequent Order Form, or (b) 30 days after the end of the pilot term."

Notice window: we can accept a 60-day notice for this pilot only. Operationally preferable to keep default MSA at 90 days but carve out the pilot in the order form.

Risks/notes: 1) be explicit this is pilot-only and dollar-capped ($50k). 2) require a signature block acknowledging waiver terms to avoid ambiguity. 3) we should log this as an exception for audit/SLA reporting.

I'll attach a redline snippet and suggested clause.

Attachment: Pilot_AutoRenew_Waiver_SOW.docx (docx, 12 KB)

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot contract question — commercial proposal

Thanks Rishi — that language works from Legal. Priyom chiming in on commercial ops:

- Pilot waiver OK for <$50k and single term, but we should require a short 'renewal opt-in' window (we propose a 30-day notice from Acme if they want to convert to production terms) so Finance has time for invoicing and resource planning.
- For bookkeeping: mark the pilot as non-recurring revenue; account team to tag deal in HubSpot as "pilot-exception".
- I suggest we add a simple sentence in the order form: "Customer must provide written notice of intent to convert to a paid agreement at least 30 days prior to pilot end for production conversion pricing to apply."

If that is acceptable, I'll prepare the non-substantive commercial redline and send to Jenny for signature.

Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Jenny / Tom — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and next steps so we can close this by EOW: 

1) Auto-renew: We will grant a one-time, pilot-specific waiver of the MSA auto-renew provision for the Acme 6-month pilot (<= $50k). Rishi has drafted language to be added to the Order Form; this does not amend the MSA broadly and will be marked as a pilot exception.

2) Notice window: We will accept a 60-day renewal notice for this pilot only. To help both teams operationally, Redwood requests that Acme provide a written intent to convert at least 30 days before pilot end (this allows Finance/Onboarding to plan).

3) Documentation: Priyom will upload the commercial redline to the Drive folder and share a DocuSign link. We'll include a signature line acknowledging the pilot waiver clause.

4) Timeline: Priyom to send redline + DocuSign by EOD today. Jenny, once you sign we will schedule kick-off for Aug 15.

If acceptable, please reply with a one-line approval and Priyom will route the DocuSign.

Best —
Neha Kapoor
